stories.headline: Silovs stops 26 as the Penguins shut out the Panthers 4-0 to end a four-game skid
stories.summary: Arturs Silovs made 26 saves and the Penguins beat Florida 4-0 at PPG Paints Arena on Thursday night, ending a four-game losing streak. Pittsburgh (4-6-1) had gone 1-6-1 in its previous eight games and had allowed at least five goals in each of the four straight losses. Nick Robertson scored twice, including an empty-netter, and Evgeni Malkin and Hendrix Lapierre each had a goal and an assist. Florida failed to get a shot on goal during a four-minute power play after Silovs took a double minor for high-sticking Sam Bennett. Panthers rookie Cooper Black made 17 saves in his NHL debut and, at 6-foot-9, became the tallest goaltender in league history. Egor Chinakhov was a late scratch with a lower-body injury and is day to day.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo launch begins as the first pre-orders reach customers in Australia and New Zealand
stories.summary: It is already Friday in Australia and New Zealand, so the first iPhone Duo pre-orders are arriving and owners are posting early photos and impressions. Apple’s first foldable starts at $1,999, with a 5.4-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen. Apple says stores in the U.S., Canada, the UK, Australia and several other countries will have a limited number of walk-in units on launch day and expects them to sell out fast because of “extraordinary” demand. There will be no walk-in sales in France, China, Japan, India, South Korea and some other markets. Online shipping estimates slipped to January 25 shortly after pre-orders opened and have stayed there, and Apple says to check back Saturday for pickup reservations. Some Apple Stores will open early at 8 a.m. local time, with North America last in line.

stories.headline: Erika Kirk fights the defense’s proposed 2029 trial date for Charlie Kirk’s accused killer
stories.summary: Erika Kirk is asking a Utah judge to reject Tyler Robinson’s defense proposal to start his murder trial in the third quarter of 2029 and instead set a date in 2027. Her lawyers called the timeline “grossly out of line” with comparable cases, cited Utah’s guarantee of a speedy disposition for crime victims, and noted that Charlie Kirk’s two children would be seven and five by the time a verdict came under the defense schedule. They also pointed to a report that Robinson’s defense cost taxpayers about $1.6 million in its first year and asked for monthly progress reports. The defense says setting a firm date now would create “false precision” in a death penalty case. Prosecutors say they could be ready by October 2027 but proposed January 31, 2028, to avoid holiday interruptions, and expect a 17-week trial.

stories.headline: Iran says seven oil tankers were hit or struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz overnight
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported Thursday that seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz overnight, which would be the most vessels damaged in a single day since the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran on Feb. 28. Quoting the Revolutionary Guard’s navy, it said four tankers were hit while transferring oil and three more were disabled by naval mines, with no details on casualties or flags. Lloyd’s List Intelligence says tankers willing to risk the run are moving through at night in a U.S. military-protected lane near Oman with their tracking systems switched off. Saudi Aramco says flows through its East-West pipeline, which bypasses the strait, have more than tripled to 7 million barrels a day.

stories.headline: Trump says he told Vivek Ramaswamy to keep up his ad featuring Amy Acton’s estranged mother
stories.summary: President Trump on Thursday praised the “very powerful” ad Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is running, which features Democrat Amy Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, calling her a “liar.” Trump wrote on Truth Social that he suggested Ramaswamy leave it up and said the press is attacking the ad “because it’s so good!” Gov. Mike DeWine had urged Ramaswamy to take it down, though he kept his endorsement, while Vice President JD Vance has defended it. Acton’s campaign condemned the ad, and her brother called it a “despicable low.” Court records the campaign provided show Arthur’s late husband was charged with raping Acton as a child, a case that never went to trial. Told that backstory at the White House, Trump said he knew nothing about it but that “Vivek is great.”

stories.headline: Sony has stopped making its last budget 4K Blu-ray player, another blow to physical media
stories.summary: Sony has stopped shipping the UBP-X700, which it positioned as its last budget 4K Blu-ray player, according to Japanese retailer Kunkoko via FlatpanelsHD. It is listed as out of stock with no restock on Sony’s Japanese store and is already sold out at Walmart and Best Buy. The move follows PlayStation’s plan to end game disc production in 2028, and the next PlayStation is not expected to have a disc drive at all. Gizmodo notes that consoles are a poor substitute for movie collectors, since the PS5 does not support Dolby Vision or Dolby Atmos for films. Sony has also sold most of its TV business to TCL and says it will skip CES 2027. Panasonic and a few others still make players, but disc playback is likely to get more expensive and niche.

stories.headline: Apple TV’s Fleetwood Mac documentary “The Chain” finally gets a January 29 premiere date
stories.summary: Fleetwood Mac: The Chain, the Apple TV documentary first announced in November 2024, will premiere on January 29, 2027, timed to the 50th anniversary of “Rumours,” which came out on Feb. 4, 1977. It features contributions from Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, the late Christine McVie, Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks, and takes its name from the only song on the album credited to all five members. Frank Marshall, who directed the Bee Gees and Beach Boys documentaries, is behind the camera. The film starts in late 1974, when Fleetwood heard Buckingham Nicks’ “Frozen Love” at Sound City Studio in Los Angeles and invited Buckingham, and then Nicks, to join. The band’s turbulent earlier years, including the Peter Green era and the “Fake Fleetwood Mac,” are left for another day.

stories.headline: LEGO’s next free gift with purchase is Ideas 40889 Build, Paint and Play, a brick-built model-making bench
stories.summary: LEGO has unveiled 40889 Build, Paint and Play!, the latest LEGO Ideas gift with purchase, available from Oct. 28 with qualifying orders of $130 or more. It is based on fan designer Doomslizer’s winning entry in the 2025 LEGO Ideas Build Your Hobby contest and recreates miniature model-making on a cutting board, with a cutting tool, glue, paint, brushes, a decal sheet and a sprue holding a helmet and air tanks in a new cooler grey. A teal Classic Space astronaut and a small pink frog round it out, though some fans had hoped for the blue astronaut from the original design. The final version trims the piece count from 235 to 158. No end date has been announced, so it may run until stock runs out.

stories.headline: Texas county approves incentives for Tesla’s $10.1 billion “Project Crystal Sun” solar factory
stories.summary: Fort Bend County commissioners voted 4-0 on Thursday to approve four incentive agreements for Tesla’s proposed $10.1 billion solar cell and module factory near Needville, Texas, south of Houston, giving the project one of its last local approvals. The plant, known internally as Project Crystal Sun, would cover about 3,000 acres and handle everything from ingot and wafer production to finished panels, with 9,712 permanent jobs projected by 2033 and operations targeted for early 2029. The site is not locked in yet. Tesla has told the Texas Comptroller it is still weighing a competing out-of-state offer and hopes to decide by the end of 2026, and the state still has to sign off on the incentives. The factory fits Musk’s goal of 100 gigawatts a year of in-house solar cell production.

stories.headline: Man accused of knocking the head off a Marine on the Iwo Jima statue near Quantico with a sledgehammer
stories.summary: A Virginia man was arrested after police say he used a sledgehammer to knock the head off one of the Marines on the limestone Iwo Jima flag-raising statue near Marine Corps Base Quantico, causing hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage. Prince William County officers answered a vandalism call around 10:13 p.m. Wednesday at Richmond Highway and Fuller Road and say they found 27-year-old Miguel Alonso Maldonado Soriano of Stafford still striking the monument. The figure farthest to the right lost its head, another Marine has gouges across his helmet and face, and a third had the bayonet on his rifle damaged. Maldonado Soriano faces three charges, including felony destruction of property.

stories.headline: Supreme Court says student IDs can’t be used to vote in New Hampshire this November, a win for Republicans
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday granted New Hampshire’s emergency request, backed by the Republican National Committee, and ruled that student IDs cannot be used at the polls in the Nov. 3 midterms. A state law passed in April already removed student IDs from the list of accepted primary identification, and Secretary of State David Scanlan, a Republican, told officials they could not be used for any purpose. U.S. District Judge Joseph Laplante blocked that guidance on Oct. 2, but the justices’ unsigned order said a federal judge should not change voting rules so close to an election, so student IDs cannot be used even as backup proof of identity. The ruling lands ahead of a closely watched Senate race between Republican John E. Sununu and Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas for retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen’s seat.

stories.headline: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake in northern Tibet kills at least 16 people and topples more than 300 homes
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck China’s Tibet region at 10:33 p.m. local time Thursday, killing at least 16 people and injuring 32, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua, citing local officials. More than 300 homes collapsed. The U.S. Geological Survey placed the epicenter about 119 miles east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude part of northern Tibet, at a depth of about 11 miles. State broadcaster CCTV called it the region’s biggest quake in five years. It comes less than two months after a glacier collapse set off flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border that killed hundreds of people.

stories.headline: Tesla is building its own AI maps for FSD navigation, with voice routing, in time for v15
stories.summary: On Tesla’s Q3 earnings call, AI chief Ashok Elluswamy answered an owner question about FSD navigation problems such as speed limits, parking and odd routing by saying Tesla “shouldn’t be depending on external people’s maps” and is building its own. He described an all-new, AI-based mapping and navigation system that owners can talk to, ask for different routes, and that learns personal and fleet-wide preferences. He said it should be ready by the time FSD v15 starts reaching customers and will take over navigation, parking and destination handling over the next several months. Tesla currently relies on Google for map data, and routing remains one of owners’ most common FSD complaints. Electrek noted the shift comes after years of Musk calling map-dependent self-driving brittle.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo, 24 hours in: great multitasking and a sturdy inner screen, but no telephoto, weaker selfies and a slower Touch ID
stories.summary: MacRumors videographer Dan Barbera got his iPhone Duo a day before Friday’s launch and answered readers’ most common questions. Some apps already have special modes for the foldable, such as a Netflix half-fold view, while unupdated apps run with thick black bars, a problem he expects to shrink as updates arrive starting Friday. Side-by-side multitasking is genuinely useful, and the inner screen feels durable, like an iPad nano-texture display, though it picks up fingerprints. The trade-offs: the camera is roughly iPhone 17 level with no telephoto, the under-display selfie camera is only fine for casual FaceTime, Touch ID has a deliberate touch-and-hold pause that is slower than Face ID, and the phone is heavy and harder to use left-handed. It starts at $1,999.

stories.headline: Microsoft says its AI diagnosed hard medical cases more than twice as accurately as doctors, in a study now published in Science
stories.summary: Microsoft’s AI Diagnostic Orchestrator, MAI-DxO, got 83.2% of complex New England Journal of Medicine case studies right, compared with 36.1% for generalist physicians who had reference materials and about 22% for those without them, according to a peer-reviewed paper published Thursday in Science. In a separate test on emergency-room admissions it again beat doctors, 80.3% to 46.8%, and Microsoft says it ordered fewer tests, at half to a third of the estimated cost. The best results came using OpenAI’s GPT-5 models. The researchers say the gap would likely narrow in real practice, and the cost savings were estimated from simulated cases. Clinical testing is set to begin at Boston’s Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center within the next couple of months.

stories.headline: Penguins lose Bryan Rust for at least six weeks with a lower-body injury, and McGroarty is called up
stories.summary: Bryan Rust will be reevaluated in six weeks after the lower-body injury that knocked him out of Monday’s 5-4 loss in Utah, coach Dan Muse said Thursday. The Penguins put Rust on injured reserve along with Ben Kindel, who is recovering after a vasovagal episode on the team plane, and recalled forward Rutger McGroarty and defenseman Chase Pietila from Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. At the morning skate before Thursday’s home game against Florida, Tommy Novak moved to left wing on Sidney Crosby’s top line, with Rickard Rakell shifting to the right, Hendrix Lapierre took the second-line center spot and Blake Lizotte replaced Kindel on the third line. Pittsburgh is 1-6-1 in its last eight games and has allowed at least five goals in four straight losses. Rust, 34, had five points in seven games.

stories.headline: Ex-Slipknot percussionist Chris Fehn authenticates his own $15,000 mask on “Pawn Stars”
stories.summary: On Wednesday’s episode of History’s “Pawn Stars,” a seller named Spencer brought Chumlee an early Slipknot Liar mask with the long nose, a drum head and a guitar said to be signed by the band’s classic lineup. He wanted $15,000 for the mask and $20,000 for the other two pieces, which he said came from an Iowa radio DJ. Chumlee joked that the mask “looks like a Halloween costume” and called in former Slipknot member Chris Fehn. Fehn remembered signing the guitar, marked “Slipknot Music Land Southridge Mall July 1999,” at one of the band’s first signings, and said the autographs, including an older version of his own signature, were real. He confirmed the mask was made for him but said he never wore it live because it didn’t fit right, which is why it is in such good shape.

stories.headline: Norway’s record Viking hoard yields a coin of King Olaf Haraldsson, the first of its kind found since 1924
stories.summary: Excavations at the Mørstad Hoard, found by metal detectorists at Rena in Norway’s Innlandet county in April, have now turned up about 5,500 Viking Age coins. One of them is inscribed ONLAF R+ NORMANORV, “Olaf, King of the Norwegians,” the University of Oslo’s Museum of Cultural History announced. It shows a bust in a conical battle helmet on one side and a cross with a Christian acclamation on the other. Olaf Haraldsson ruled Norway from 1015 to 1028 and drove the country’s conversion to Christianity. Fewer than 20 of his coins survive, most of them outside Norway, and none like this one had been found since 1924. An archaeologist on the dig called it a national treasure, and experts say Olaf may have chosen the design himself.

stories.headline: Trumbull’s Kids Pumpkin Fest is Sunday on the Town Hall Green with pumpkin decorating, a live DJ and touch-a-truck
stories.summary: Trumbull’s annual Kids Pumpkin Fest runs this Sunday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the Town Hall Green at 5866 Main Street, Patch reports. The free family event features pumpkin decorating, face painting, lawn games, crafts and a live DJ, plus a touch-a-truck with the Long Hill Fire and Trumbull Police departments and crafts with the Trumbull Nature and Arts Center. Mobile coffee trailer Brewberry Cafe will serve a seasonal menu.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.
